# claude-decisions-mod

A [Claude Code mod](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview) that
decides, before a tool call runs, whether it may: deterministic guards for the
Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep and Glob tools, and a model-assisted second
opinion from a **decision model** ([Jev](https://vercel.com/kb/jev-from-typesafe-ai)
by TypeSafe AI on [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/modalities/decision))
for the long tail of risky commands no rule enumerates.

It is the TypeScript port of the Python hooks in
[`jessearmand/claude-code-rules`](https://github.com/jessearmand/claude-code-rules)
(`hooks/*.py`), rewritten as a hooks module that runs inside Claude Code
instead of as settings-hook scripts. Policy, rule ids, reason texts and the
bash-subset parser are the same; see [docs/PORTING.md](docs/PORTING.md) for
the module map and the conventions of the port.

[cc-safety-net](https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net) is the reference for
guard-family coverage. PowerShell and Windows shells are out of scope: the
guards cover Bash on Linux and macOS.

## Install

At the prompt of a Claude Code terminal session:

```
/plugin install decisions-guard --marketplace jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod
```

From a shell:

```
claude plugin install decisions-guard --marketplace jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod
```

In the Desktop app, where `/plugin` does not run: click **+** next to the
prompt box, then **Plugins**, **Add marketplace** with
`jessearmand/claude-decisions-mod`, then **Add plugin**.

To run it from a checkout for one session: `claude --plugin-dir /path/to/claude-decisions-mod`.

Do not also wire the Python hooks of `claude-code-rules` in `settings.json`:
every call would be judged twice.

## What it decides

Every guard answers `deny` or `ask` or defers to the normal permission flow;
none ever answers `allow`, so your own permission rules are never loosened.
A deny from any guard wins over an ask; the model is consulted only when
nothing deterministic decided, and it can only ask.

| Guard | Tools | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `rm-rf-guard` | Bash | Asks before any `rm` that is both recursive and forced, with a per-target analysis and the least destructive alternative. |
| `dangerous-commands` | Bash | Denies (or asks about) destructive git, downloads piped into a shell, disk writes, `chmod -R 777`, crontab, package publishing, cloud/Kubernetes/database deletes and switching off security controls. Local removals (`git clean -f`, `find -delete`, `shred`) ask. |
| `secrets-guard` | Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob | Blocks reading, mutating or exfiltrating credential files (`.env`, keys, cloud and coding-agent tokens), in three tiers. |
| `config-guard` | Bash, Edit, Write | Stops the agent changing its own settings, hooks, MCP servers, other harnesses' config, home-directory skills and instructions, and persistence locations (shell rc files, git hooks and config, launchd, systemd, cron). |
| `file-protection` | Edit, Write | Denies hand edits to generated files: lockfiles, `.git/` internals, `node_modules/`. |
| `bash-command-validator` | Bash | Points `grep`, `find -name` and source-code `rg` at `rg`, `rg --files` and `ast-grep`. |
| `bash-risk-judge` | Bash | Opt-in. Asks a decision model typed questions (destruction, exfiltration, persistence, weakened controls, fetch-and-execute, privilege escalation, erased history, credential stores, network exposure, off-task) and prompts when any crosses a threshold. |

All Bash guards parse the command with a shared bash-subset parser, so
newlines, `sudo -u x`, `timeout 5`, `bash -c`, `eval`, `ssh host '...'`,
`$(...)`, heredocs fed to a shell and interpreter one-liners cannot hide a
command, and what a command runs from disk (shell scripts, `npm run`
scripts, Makefile recipes, database command files, git aliases) is read and
judged too. A match found only in such a file asks instead of denying.

Under `bypassPermissions` or `dontAsk`, where nobody can answer, a
deterministic ask becomes a deny (set `unattendedKeepAsk` to keep asks).
The mode is read from the merged settings' `permissions.defaultMode`.

## The Jev risk judge

The judge is off until enabled. It sends the (redacted) command, the
user's latest prompt, the agent's last few commands and the body of any
script the command runs to `POST https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/evaluate`
with typed boolean and choice questions, and reads back calibrated
probabilities. Credentials are, in order: the `jevApiKey` option,
`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`, or `fnox` (pointed at
`HOOK_JEV_FNOX_CONFIG`). Every failure (no key, timeout, bad JSON) defers.

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `{ "name": "<mod-name>", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "<one line>" }`
- `hooks/hooks.json`: `{ "modules": ["./register.tsx"] }`, one path, relative to that file
- `hooks/register.tsx` (or `.ts`): the hooks module, `export const register: Register = (on, options) => { ... }`, the type imported from `'claude-code'`

A mod that keeps values in `$.state` has a fourth file, `types/index.d.ts`: its type contract, declaring each value in `interface PluginState` under the mod's name, named in `plugin.json` as `"types": "./types/index.d.ts"`. The module imports its value types from `'../types'`, and `claude plugin validate` holds every `$.state` key the module names to that contract.

WHERE THE TYPES ARE. The engine writes them; there is no command to run. Before the mod has loaded: `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring/types/claude-code.d.ts`, this build's API and built-in tools, written as this skill loaded (this process's own folder: after a restart the next load of this skill writes and names a new one). Once the engine has loaded the mod (from this mods folder, or a `--plugin-dir` folder it hot-reloads), `<mod folder>/.claude-plugin/types/` holds the same for the editor: `claude-code/index.d.ts`, the API; `claude-code-tools/index.d.ts`, so `e.tool === "Bash"` narrows `e`; `claude-code-mcp/index.d.ts`, the MCP tools connected when the mod last reloaded; each `dependencies` plugin's contract; and a `tsconfig.json` the mod's own extends, so `tsc -p <mod folder>` type-checks it. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE TURN ENDS. Loading this skill through the Skill tool or its slash command starts the engine's watch on the folder that holds the mod folders. The first file written under it makes the engine ask the person, once, right then, while the turn goes on: "Enable hot reloading for this session?", with `How does this work?` first, then `Enable for this session` and `Not now`. That question is the switch, and the person alone answers it: no permission mode, rule or hook does. On `Enable for this session` the folder joins the session's plugin folders and the mod loads when the turn ends, whole, and each later edit reloads it when the turn that made the edit ends. The answer reaches you as a notice at the start of your next turn, one of: enabled, with what the load came to; declined (the mods are written and load the next time this session starts; the person can ask for the question again); still open (a new prompt from the person takes the question down, and the engine asks again when that turn ends); or off, with the reason (nobody could be asked, as under `claude -p`; the question got no pick three times; an organization's policy; an untrusted workspace). `on(event, matcher?, hook)` adds a hook, and every hook is `($, e, next)`: `$` is the engine interface, each call spelled noun then method; `e` is the event's input, a plain frozen value; `next(e)` runs the plugins beneath and then the engine's own behaviour, resolving to the event's result. `register` runs again in a fresh environment and the previous environment's timers are dropped. A save that leaves a loaded file holding the text it was loaded from reloads nothing (after a reload that failed, any new save tries again). Saves made while the session's own turn runs (the model editing the plugin) reload once, when the turn ends, or sooner when a tool or command the plugin registered is about to run, so the turn can try what it wrote. Saves from anywhere else reload once the folder has been quiet: a lone save within a quarter second, a run of saves seconds apart once the run stops. A headless `claude -p` always loads fresh, and a long-lived headless session (SDK, desktop) watches too when `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=1` is set the same way, its reload lines reaching the host as `ui_log` messages and the debug log.
Options for a plugin loaded this way are read from settings under `pluginConfigs`, keyed by the plugin's `<name>` (or `<name>@inline`); each non-secret `userConfig` field is a row in the config menu too, and a change there reloads the module with the new `options`. A `string` field that lists `options` (`"options": ["gist", "turbo"]`, its `default` among them) is a picker over exactly those values there, and a stored value outside them counts as unset.

An installed plugin is read from one of two places, and `/reload-plugins` re-reads that place. A plugin whose marketplace is a folder (`claude plugin marketplace add <folder>`) and whose entry there is a relative path (`"source": "./mods/tally"`) is read from that folder itself, never from the copy `claude plugin install` made: edit the folder, run `/reload-plugins`, and the reload names it and the folder when the folder changed since the session last read it (`<plugin>@<marketplace>` re-read from its folder: `<folder>`), in a terminal and in a session the desktop app hosts on this machine alike, with no new version and no reinstall; `claude plugin update` says it is read from its folder when the folder holds the version on record, and `claude plugin list` shows the folder (`Read from:`). Every other installed plugin runs the copy made when it was installed (a git, npm or archive source, a marketplace fetched from a repository or a URL): an edit to a working copy reaches a session only as a new version or commit, through `claude plugin update` and then `/reload-plugins`. The folder a reload or the list names is the one the session runs: where that is not the working copy (the desktop app keeps a plugin saved from an upload in a folder of its own), add the working copy's folder as a marketplace and install from it, or name it in `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`. A plugin folder given as a link is watched at the folder the link names.

You wanted to clarify my two questions, so I've stopped there. Nothing is installed, your settings are unchanged, and nothing is committed. Here is where things stand.

## Linter and formatter: Biome replaced by oxlint and oxfmt
- **Removed:** `biome.json` and `@biomejs/biome`.
- **Formatter:** `.oxfmtrc.json` came from `oxfmt --migrate=biome`, so it keeps 4-space indent, 110 columns and double quotes. I excluded `*.md`, because Biome never formatted Markdown and oxfmt would rewrite every table. Running it reformatted 3 files slightly (`engine-host.ts`, `writes.ts`, `package.json`).
- **Scripts:** `lint` now runs `oxlint --deny-warnings && oxfmt --check`. `format` runs `oxfmt`. There is a new `lint:fix`.
- **Two small fixes the linter asked for:** `new Array(n)` in `scripts/script-support.ts` and a redundant length check in `scripts/judge-probe.ts`.
- **Old suppression comments:** The `biome-ignore` comments are now plain comments. They kept their explanation, such as "a shell spelling of HOME, not a template".
- **README:** updated the dev commands. I also fixed the credential order it listed. The code reads the `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` and `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` environment variables before the `jevApiKey` option, not after.

**About the side note:** it's right that oxlint now checks less than Biome did. `.oxlintrc.json` turns on only the correctness rules, and switches off four rules for these reasons:
- **Control characters in regex:** Biome had this rule off too.
- **Needless spread:** a false alarm. At `src/shell/unwrap.ts:188` the spread splits a string into characters, and the other hits copy a Map's keys on purpose before deleting from it.
- **`expect` inside conditions:** the table-driven tests rely on it.
- **`expect` argument limit:** raised to 2, because vitest accepts `expect(value, message)`.

Adding the suspicious rules as warnings turns up about 150 hits. 77 of them flag `${...}` in plain strings, mostly tests that spell shell syntax on purpose; Biome needed only 13 suppressions for the same thing. The rest are 26 shadowed variables, 21 `.sort()` calls and 14 functions that could move out of their parent. Since `lint` fails on any warning, turning that group on means working through all of it first. I'd do that as a separate change.

## Checks
All pass: oxlint, oxfmt, 7,648 vitest tests, `tsc`, `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin test` (7/7).
- **Tests:** two `config-guard` tests were already failing before my changes, only on macOS. The temp folder `/var/...` is a link to `/private/var/...`, which added an extra path form. I fixed the test setup to resolve the real temp path; the guard code was correct.
- **Typecheck:** it needs `.claude-plugin/types`, a git-ignored folder that Claude Code writes when it loads the mod. This checkout didn't have it yet, so I copied this build's types in.

## Jev with ai 0.7
The new version works with the existing client unchanged. The gateway lists `typesafe-ai/jev`, `jev-1.13.0` and `jev-1.14.0`. The fnox lookup also works with no key in the environment: I ran the judge from `/`, it found the key, and there were 0 errors.

| p95 latency | 0.73s | 0.63s |
| Backup provider | DigitalOcean | none |

The alias's answers differ from 1.14.0's, so it most likely still serves the older 1.13 weights. I left the default as the alias.

"Classic" means the settings-file hook system: the `hooks` block in `settings.json`, with events like `PreToolUse`, `Stop` and `Notification`. The mod API exposes each of those events as `classic.<Name>`. Yes, there is a newer, mod-native event for the same moment: `tool.call`. I took all of this from the engine's type file that Claude Code 2.1.302 wrote into `.claude-plugin/types/claude-code/index.d.ts`.

**How the two events nest.** `tool.call` is the outer event, and `classic.PreToolUse` runs inside it:

```
tool.call hooks (every plugin)          ← the newer event
  └─ next(e) → core:
       classic.PreToolUse chain         ← where decisions-guard is
         [managed hooks, mod hooks, your settings hooks]
       → permission prompt / auto-mode classifier
       → the tool itself
```

| | `classic.PreToolUse` (current) | `tool.call` |
|---|---|---|
| Results | `allow` / **`ask`** / `deny`, or nothing (normal permission flow) | `{ deny }`, or `{ result }` (answer for the tool) |
| Can prompt you | Yes. `ask` opens Claude Code's own permission dialog, the same as the Python hooks. | No `ask` result. The nearest thing is `$.ui.ask(…)`, a separate question dialog. It fails in `-p` runs, and auto mode's classifier doesn't take part. |
| What it wraps | Only the decision | Everything: the permission check, the prompt and the tool's result. It can rewrite input, change output, or act after the tool ran. |
| Organization-managed Claude Code | Skipped for plugins a person installs (`plugin validate` warned about this) | Runs |

**My recommendation: stay on `classic.PreToolUse`.** Asking is the core of this mod. `rm-rf-guard` always asks, file removals like `git clean -f` ask, and the Jev judge can only ask. `tool.call` has no ask result, so a move would mean building prompts on `$.ui.ask`. That loses the real permission dialog and the auto-mode behaviour, and needs its own fallback where nobody can answer. `tool.call` becomes worth it only if you want things PreToolUse can't do, such as hiding secrets in tool output after the tool ran, or running on organization-managed machines. Even then, a mixed design is better: keep the decisions on `classic.PreToolUse` and add a `tool.call` hook only for the after-the-tool part.

**Your model change** is saved as `jevModel: typesafe-ai/jev-1.14.0` in `pluginConfigs`, and the judge has been running since your reload. I can't prove from the log that 1.14.0 answered, because the audit log doesn't record which model it asked. Two reminders from the earlier probe: 1.14.0 has no backup provider, and it sometimes asks about `terraform plan`. If those asks annoy you, raise `askThreshold` to 0.75.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Your mod's hooks sit in the middle of the chain: below managed hooks, above your own settings hooks. A deny from a managed hook still overrules the mod, and the mod overrules anything you add to `settings.json` later.
- `tool.call` guards fail open by default: if the hook fails, it is skipped and the tool runs. That's why `register.ts` adds `.catch(...)` to deny when `next` wasn't called. Any `tool.call` hook you add later needs the same.

I checked all five codex findings against the engine's own type definitions and the code. All five were real, and all five are now fixed, each with a regression test. Nothing is committed yet.

| # | What codex said | What I found | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** symlinks in globs | `$.fs.list()` reports a link as `other`. Our `Host` expects what the link points to. | Confirmed: the engine docs say "A symbolic link is `other`". So a glob like `al*/settings.json` never went through a linked `~/.claude`, and config-guard let the write through. | `listDirectory` in `src/host/engine-host.ts` now looks up each link with `$.fs.stat`, which follows it. A broken link stays `other`. |
| **P1** case aliases | The case test needed `realPath` to fold case. | Confirmed: the engine docs say "a case alias keeps its own spelling". So `~/.CLAUDE/SETTINGS.JSON` looked like a case-sensitive disk and skipped the settings rules. | `caseInsensitive` in `src/shell/filesystem-paths.ts` now only checks that the case-swapped name exists. On a case-sensitive disk that only happens when a separate sibling exists, and then it errs towards more protection. |
| **P2** slow matching | `fnmatch` retried every `*`, so time grew exponentially. | Confirmed, and it was worse than reported: bash `match` (used for `${X#pat}` and similar), which runs as a regex, blew up too. 10 stars on 40 characters took 6.2 s in `fnmatch` and 0.65 s in `match`. | New `src/shell/wildcard.ts` with a matcher that only ever retries the last `*`. Its time is bounded by text length × pattern length. Both matchers use it, and both now run in about 0 ms. Patterns with extglob groups (only after `shopt -s extglob`) still use the regex. |
| **P2** lost log records | Two log appends running at once could each read the file, then overwrite each other. | Confirmed with a fake `$.fs`: records went missing. | A queue per log path holds the whole read-then-write, so each append waits for the one before it. |
| **P2** `askInsteadOfDeny` ignored | secrets-guard never applied it. | Confirmed: `askForLevel` ignored `askAll`. | `askAll` now applies to all three levels in `src/config.ts`. dangerous-commands already asked, so nothing changes there. |

**Tests:** all checks pass: typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and 7,665 vitest tests (6 new). `claude plugin test` passed 7/7 and `claude plugin validate` passed. The new engine-host and case-alias tests fail on the old code and pass on the fixed code.

**Other changed files:**
- **New spec, `src/host/engine-host.spec.ts`:** a stand-in for `$.fs` that behaves as the engine docs describe.
- **tsconfig changes:** the spec is type-checked under `tsconfig.json`, which has the engine types and no Node globals, and it is excluded from `tsconfig.node.json`.

**Two limits remain in the log writer:**
- **Other processes:** the queue only covers this mod inside one Claude Code process. A second Claude Code process writing the same day's log can still lose records, because the engine has no atomic append or file lock.
- **Large logs (separate bug):** `appendTextTo` only reads the existing log while it is under 3 MiB. Past that it writes `"" + record`, which wipes the whole day's log. The fix could be to start a numbered file for the day or to skip the write. Which one is your call, so I left it alone.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Read the engine contract, not the other hosts:** the two P1 bugs came from writing the engine adapter as if it behaved like the Node and in-memory hosts. The engine docs state both differences.
- **A glob only needs to retry its last `*`:** every other token matches exactly one character, so going back to an earlier star never helps. That is why one saved position replaces the exponential search.
- **Queue the whole append:** codex was right that queueing only the write isn't enough. Each append has to wait for the previous one before it reads, or it reads stale content.

**What changed** (in `appendTextTo`, `src/host/engine-host.ts`):

- **Parallel appends:** each log path still has one queue, and all the numbered files for a day go through it. So parallel calls in one session still can't lose each other's records, even when a new file starts.
- **Last resort:** if 1,000 files for one day are all full, the record is dropped and a debug line is logged. The plugin still never throws.

**Still open:** two separate Claude Code sessions writing the same day's log can still overwrite each other. The engine has no atomic append and no file lock.
